terms.definition: Living on or using land with the owner’s permission, for example under a licence or tenancy. Permission stops the clock for adverse possession.
Gaining title to land by occupying it openly, without the owner’s permission, for a period set by law: 12 years for unregistered land in England and Wales (Limitation Act 1980).
Written or spoken permission to occupy land. A licence is not ownership, and in law it stops time running for adverse possession.
The person or company named on HM Land Registry’s title register as the owner of a piece of land.
HM Land Registry’s official record of a piece of registered land: who owns it, its title plan, and any charges or rights over it.
Registering a piece of land with HM Land Registry for the first time, usually after a sale or transfer. The deeds before it are not copied onto the register.
The reference HM Land Registry gives each registered title, such as WA231076.
Outright ownership of land, held for ever, as opposed to a lease for a fixed term.
Holding land for a fixed term from the freeholder, usually in return for rent. A ground rent is the rent paid on a long lease.
A manorial title is the lordship of a manor and the rights that go with it. Land held “under a lord” was held from the lord of the manor, by lease or custom, rather than owned outright.
The deed that transfers ownership of land from one owner to another.
A court case in which an owner asks the court to order someone off land.
The 1987 Court of Appeal judgment ([1987] EWCA Civ 2) on possession of the farmhouse land at Llandough.
The second-highest court in England and Wales. It hears appeals from the High Court and county courts.
A request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000. Anyone can ask a public body for the information it holds; it must answer within 20 working days.
The Environmental Information Regulations 2004: the FOI route for information about land, the environment and planning.
A request under UK data protection law for a copy of the personal data an organisation holds about you. The answer is due within one calendar month.

learn_more.label: HM Land Registry subject access request

terms.definition: The UK regulator for Freedom of Information and data protection. A complaint goes to the ICO after a body’s internal review.
A public body’s second look at its own FOI answer, asked for by the person who made the request. It is the step before a complaint to the ICO.
Under section 1(3) of the FOI Act a body may ask for more detail before answering. The 20-working-day clock starts again when the clarification arrives.
Section 12 of the FOI Act lets a body refuse a request that would cost more than the set limit to answer.

learn_more.label: Llandough Community Council internal review of a section 12 refusal

terms.definition: The answer a public body gives when it finds no recorded information matching a request.
The local database of archaeological sites and historic buildings. Tŷ Mawr is HER GGAT02038s.
National Primary Record Number: the reference in the National Monuments Record of Wales (Coflein). Tŷ Mawr is NPRN 20182.
Land registered as a town or village green. VG41 is the green at Church View Close, Llandough.

terms.definition: The catalogue number each record has on Cedwyn, such as EV-0080 or GHF-E090. Every fact on the site points to one.
David Stewart’s 1824 survey of the Bute Glamorgan estates. Its plan 19 names “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”, the first record mention of Tŷ Mawr.
The police force for South Wales, including the Vale of Glamorgan.

terms.definition: The local council for Llandough, Penarth and the Vale; the planning authority since 1996.

terms.definition: The community council for Llandough, the lowest tier of local government.

terms.definition: National Police Chiefs’ Council: coordinates police forces in the UK and answers FOI requests about national policing.
The government department for the courts (through HMCTS), prisons and the justice system.

learn_more.label: Ministry of Justice subject access request

terms.definition: The government department for the armed forces.
Department for Culture, Media and Sport: the UK department for heritage and listed buildings policy in England.
The county record office for Cardiff and the Vale of Glamorgan, in Cardiff.
The national library in Aberystwyth. It holds the Bute estate records catalogue.
The Glamorgan landholdings of the Marquesses of Bute, sold off in the 1930s–1940s.
The study of a word or place-name’s history: its earlier forms, linguistic elements and development over time.

terms.definition: A later explanation of a name or word based on its resemblance to a familiar word, even when that resemblance does not represent the historical linguistic origin.
The adaptation of a name or word into English spelling or usage. In place-name research, the historic Welsh form and English form should be recorded separately.
A name used to identify an individual. A place-name may preserve or derive from a personal name, but that connection needs a source-based linguistic argument.

terms.definition: A name assigned to a geographical feature or human settlement. Historical spellings and their source locators help distinguish documented forms from later interpretations.
